scholarships.title: Canada Graduate Research Scholarship—Doctoral (CGRS-D)
scholarships.official_source: Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC)

existing.description: The Canada Graduate Research Scholarship-Doctoral program recognises and supports the next generation of outstanding innovators, knowledge workers, creative thinkers and researchers, providing support for a high-quality research training experience. For the October 2026 competition SSHRC publishes a value and duration of $40,000 per year for 3 years. There are two application routes: direct to SSHRC by October 19, 2026 (8:00 p.m. eastern), or through a Canadian institution, which the page warns often closes significantly earlier than the agency deadline.
eligibility: Enrolled in, or applying to, a doctoral programme in Canada
Apply either directly to SSHRC by the agency deadline or through a Canadian institution, which often has a significantly earlier deadline
Doctoral applicants in the health, natural and social sciences, engineering and humanities are reached through SSHRC as one of the three federal research agencies
existing.eligibility_summary: The programme recognises and supports the next generation of outstanding innovators, knowledge workers, creative thinkers and researchers, providing support for a high-quality research training experience. Applications are made either directly to SSHRC or through a Canadian institution.
benefits: Eligible for affiliated fellowships and supplements
For additional information, see the description of the Indigenous Scholars Awards and Supplements Pilot Initiative.
requirements: Application through CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC portal
Research proposal aligned with agency mandate
Letter of Appraisal form—Instructions for referees
existing.english_requirement: other than English or French, you must provide a certified English or French translation.
application_method: Submit directly to SSHRC by October 19, 2026 (8:00 p.m. eastern), or apply through a Canadian institution
For direct applications, the SSHRC page links separate Applicant instructions and a Letter of Appraisal form with instructions for referees
A Letter of Appraisal by the research supervisor is part of the direct-application route
existing.selection_notes: Merit-based; evaluated by agency-specific peer review committees. Automatically considered for affiliated fellowships at some institutions.
existing.best_fit: Outstanding doctoral students pursuing research careers across all disciplines.
existing.notes: Replaces the former CGSD program under the harmonized CRTAS suite. Distinct from the Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarship.
existing.deadline_display: Application deadlines: Directly to SSHRC: October 19, 2026 (8:00 p.m. eastern). Through a Canadian institution: contact your institution, often significantly earlier than the agency's deadline.
existing.program_type: Federal research training award (Canada Graduate Research Scholarship program)

scholarships.title: Ontario Graduate Scholarship (OGS) - University of Toronto
scholarships.official_source: School of Graduate Studies, University of Toronto / Ontario Ministry of Colleges, Universities, Research Excellence and Security

existing.description: The Ontario Graduate Scholarship program encourages excellence in graduate studies at publicly-assisted universities in Ontario and has provided merit-based scholarships to Ontario's best graduate students in all disciplines since 1975. At the University of Toronto the program is jointly funded by the Province of Ontario and the University of Toronto, and the Province allocates OGS awards to universities specifying how many each may offer annually. The OGS is worth $5,000 per session at U of T, and the awarding graduate unit contributes one-third of the total award cost. Deadlines and application dates are set by each graduate unit, with results in mid-July.
eligibility: Canadian citizen, Permanent Resident or Protected Person under subsection 95(2) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (Canada) by the graduate unit's student deadline

International student on a temporary resident visa (study permit) at U of T - eligible for a set number of OGS awards, with a valid study permit effective as of the graduate unit's OGS international application deadline
Registered or intending to register full-time in an eligible programme in 2026-2027; a full-time student is one in at least 60% of a full course load (40% for students with a permanent disability)
Have not exceeded the lifetime maximum of government-funded support or the maximum OGS/QEII support available for the current level of study
At least A- (or equivalent) in each of the last two completed years of study, or an overall A- average on all graduate courses if two or more years of graduate study are complete
Must be in good standing with the Ontario Student Assistance Program (OSAP)
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be a Canadian citizen, Permanent Resident or Protected Person under subsection 95(2) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (Canada) by the student deadline set by each graduate unit, or an international student studying or planning to study at U of T under a temporary resident visa (student study permit), for whom a limited number of OGS awards are available and whose valid study permits must be effective as of the graduate unit's OGS international application deadline. Applicants must be registered or intend to register full-time in 2026-2027 in an eligible two- or three-term graduate programme, must not have exceeded the lifetime maximum of government-funded support, and must have achieved at least A- (or equivalent) in each of the last two completed years of study.
benefits: Automatic consideration for the SGS Inclusive Excellence Graduate Scholarship competition for graduate students who are Black and/or Indigenous to Canada and identify as such on the OGS application, with OGS awards valued at up to $15,000 per year
Approximately 25 awards made available annually through the Inclusive Excellence Graduate Scholarship opportunity
coverage: OGS value of $5,000 per session, giving $10,000 for two consecutive sessions or $15,000 for three consecutive sessions
The awarding graduate unit contributes one-third of the total award cost in all instances
Payments are issued through ACORN in equal instalments at the start of each academic session
requirements: Submit an OGS application to the proposed graduate unit using the SGS centralized online OGS application
Meet the graduate unit's own internal submission deadline
application_method: Complete the SGS centralized online OGS application and submit it to the proposed graduate unit
Provide transcripts from all post-secondary institutions (unofficial student-issued transcripts such as ACORN screenshots are permitted)
Provide a plan of study of a maximum of 2 pages (1 page plan, 1 page references/citations)
Provide two academic references, who will be required to submit online
existing.selection_notes: University-specific internal deadlines apply. Applications are first adjudicated at the university level, then forwarded to a centralized provincial competition.
existing.best_fit: Graduate students with strong academic records seeking merit-based funding at Ontario universities.
existing.notes: International students are eligible for a set number of awards at each university. Cannot be combined with certain other government awards beyond lifetime maximums.
existing.duration: Each scholarship is tenable for one year, i.e. two consecutive or three academic sessions.
existing.application_period: University-specific internal deadlines; provincial competition annually
existing.deadline_display: Student Deadline: date set by graduate unit. Application Dates: determined by graduate unit. Graduate Unit Deadline: refer to SGS Memo. Results: mid-July.
